summary: This note describes Billy Joel's song "Christmas in Fallujah", written in September 2007 after he read letters from American soldiers in Iraq. Joel premiered it on December 1, 2007, with Cass Dillon singing the studio recording, and dedicated it to servicemen based in Iraq. On December 11, 2008, Joel recorded his own live version at Acer Arena in Sydney, released as an Australia-only live single, and proceeds from the song benefited Homes For Our Troops.
one_line: Billy Joel's 2007 song "Christmas in Fallujah" for servicemen in Iraq and his 2008 live Australian recording of it.
key_facts: Joel wrote "Christmas in Fallujah" in September 2007 after reading numerous letters sent to him from American soldiers in Iraq.
On December 1, 2007, Joel premiered his new song "Christmas in Fallujah".
Cass Dillon, a new Long Island based musician, performed the song on the 2007 studio recording because Joel felt it should be sung by someone in a soldier's age range.
The track was dedicated to servicemen based in Iraq.
Proceeds from "Christmas in Fallujah" benefited the Homes For Our Troops foundation.
"Christmas in Fallujah" is only the second pop/rock song released by Joel since 1993's River of Dreams.
On December 11, 2008, Joel recorded his own rendition of "Christmas in Fallujah" during a concert at Acer Arena in Sydney.
Joel's 2008 rendition was released as a live single in Australia only.
It is the only official release of Joel performing "Christmas in Fallujah".
Cass Dillon sang on the 2007 studio recording and the handful of times the song was played live in 2007.
Joel himself has played the song occasionally in concert.
Joel sang "Christmas in Fallujah" throughout his December 2008 tour of Australia.
